newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish lackluster day lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish lackluster day lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended lower after a very quiet session, pressured by jitters before Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday and upcoming supply.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will deliver his semiannual address on the state of the U.S. economy to the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday. His testimony to the House Banking Committee was postponed until March 5 from Thursday.
"Greenspan, weak technicals and supply are all coming together at one time," said Don Pullen, ED and F Man's trading floor manager for T-bonds.
Treasury will auction $17.5 billion in two-year notes on Tuesday and $12.5 billion in five-year notes on Wednesday.

"We opened beneath support at 112-24/32 and we just couldn't recover," Pullen said. "We did find support off of 112-14/32 but we could not really get much going from the weak opening and it suggests the market remains on the defensive," Pullen said. He said lower levels could prevail into the week.
Strong support rests at 112-3/32 to 112-5/32, some technicans said.
"It was kind of a dud day again," a T-bond options trader said. "We're not having very broad ranges."

Another T-bond options trader said the market could languish into midweek and then stage a "relief rally" after Greenspan's first leg of testimony is complete. Others said the market could remain rangebound until his second day of testimony.
John Nyhoff, chief economist for Mitusbishi Financial Futures, said most of what the market will be interested in should come from Greenspan's written commentary, released Wednesday.
"The delay isn't really going to keep the market in suspended animation for the extra week," Nyhoff said.
Any differences in Greenspan's testimony will likely be in the question-and-answer sessions to the committees, not in the testimony itself, Nyhoff said.
Bond options sources noted paper buying of about 5,000 June 112 bond calls.

At the end of pit trading, March T-bonds were down 10/32 at 112-20/32, T-notes eased 5/32 to 109-17/32, muni-bonds lost 7/32 to 116-30/32, June T-bills were flat at 94.94, and June Eurodollars lost one basis point to 94.39. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
